transcript.text: My Dyson V10 Absolute (SV12) won't run at all now. On the battery display there's a red light flashing when I press the trigger, then nothing. It was charging overnight. Do I need a new battery or is the whole thing dead?

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. A flashing red light on a Dyson V10 when pressing the trigger usually indicates a battery communication error, a deeply discharged battery, or a fault with the charger/battery interface. It doesn't necessarily mean the whole vacuum is dead, but it does point to a power issue. Before assuming the battery needs replacing, we need to check if the charging system is working correctly: 1. Check the charging light: Plug the V10 into its dock and ensure the socket is live (try another device in that socket). Look at the light on the battery itself. Does it turn solid green/amber to show charging? Or does it stay flashing red?
2. Check for blockages: Even if the battery is charged, a severe blockage can trip a safety cut-out. Detach the wand and floorhead from the main body. Look through the tube and check the bin inlet for any obstructions (coins, debris). Ensure the filters are clean and completely dry. Please let me know what happens with the charging light first, as that is the most critical clue.

The charger light is on and I tried another socket too, same result. While it's on the charger the blue lights come on, then it sometimes shows the flashing red as well. Filter was washed last month, bin's empty and no blockages. Battery isn't swollen, hot or smelly either.

The fact that you see blue lights then a flashing red while charging suggests the battery is either deeply discharged (it hasn't reached a safe voltage yet) or one of the cells has failed internally, preventing the pack from accepting a full charge. Since the charger light is on and the socket is good, we need to distinguish between 'needs more time' and 'won't hold charge'. Please leave it on the dock for a full 3.5 hours (Dyson chargers typically take this long for a V10). Do not try to use it during this time. After 3.5 hours:
1. Take the battery off the dock.
2. Press the trigger to turn it on. If it runs normally: The battery was just deeply discharged and is now recovered.
If the red light flashes immediately or it won't start: The battery has likely failed and needs replacement, as it can no longer hold a charge despite charging time.

I already did the 3.5 hour charge, plugged straight into the battery rather than the dock. Blue lights came on while charging, but it still flashes red when I press the trigger and the motor won't start. So is it the battery that's failed? It's the original, about 4.5 years old.

[Heading: Likely cause: battery — flat or failed (cordless)]
Here is why: Your V10 is 4.5 years old and still on its original battery. Lithium-ion batteries typically last 3 to 5 years before their capacity drops significantly or they develop internal faults that prevent them from holding a charge. The flashing red light after a full charge, combined with the motor refusing to start, is the standard indicator for a battery that can no longer deliver power. Filters, and charging socket issues, there is no further owner-safe check that will fix this. You will need to replace the battery pack. 1. Order a replacement battery for your Dyson V10 (SV12). Ensure it is compatible with your specific model.
2. Once you have the new battery, remove the old one and insert the new one. The red light should stop flashing when you press the trigger, and the vacuum should run normally. If you are not comfortable replacing the battery yourself, or if the vacuum still does not work after installing a new battery (which would suggest a fault with the main motor or electronics), then you will need to contact Dyson support or an appliance engineer.

candidates: Battery or charging fault (flat/failed battery or charger issue) (high)
Thermal cut-out tripped due to blockage or overheating (medium)
Internal fault (motor, PCB, or battery management system) (low)
